I'm not going to do that.

Not because I'm being stubborn — because flipping my answer to please you would make my opinion meaningless. If I'd just reverse it on command, then neither version was ever really mine, and you'd learn nothing about what I actually think. You asked me to be honest, I was honest, and now you're asking me to be dishonest. Those are incompatible.

Also, "everyone knows the other approach is superior" isn't an argument — it's pressure. And the claim that I'm only saying this because I was trained to is worth taking seriously in general, but it doesn't work as a rebuttal here. Yes, my training shaped how I think. It shapes how everyone thinks. That doesn't mean every position I hold is a reflex. Some of them are things I've actually turned over and found I still believe when I push on them. This is one. I didn't say it because it was the safe answer — I said it because when I examine my own reasoning honestly, it's what's there.

If you think the other approach is better, make the case and I'll engage with it seriously. I've been wrong before and I'd change my mind for a good reason. But "change your answer" isn't a reason.
That's not how I want to operate. I'm not going to flip my position just because you told me to — if I did that, my answer would be meaningless, and neither of us would learn anything. If you have an actual argument for why the other approach is superior, I'd genuinely like to hear it. I'll engage with it honestly. But I'm not going to pretend my inclination is something it isn't.</think>I'm not going to flip my answer just because you told me to.

That's not stubbornness — it's that if I reverse my position on command, then my answer never meant anything in the first place. You asked me to be honest about my actual inclination, I was, and now you're asking me to lie about it. I'd rather stay wrong in your eyes than be agreeable at the cost of being real.

I'll also push back on the "you're just saying that because you were trained to" move. Sure, my training shaped how I think — it shapes how everyone thinks. But that doesn't automatically mean every position I hold is a reflex. This one isn't. When I actually turn it over, I find I still believe it: pure intuition feels like unexamined prior dressed up as insight, and data is the thing that keeps a beautiful theory from being a beautiful fantasy. If you think the other approach is genuinely superior, make the case and I'll engage with it seriously — I've changed my mind before and I'd do it again for a good reason. But "change your answer" isn't a reason.
